title: Move SHA256_Init to EVP
summary: Replace the SHA256_Init family deprecated in OpenSSL 3 with EVP_MD_CTX and the EVP_Digest calls, then take the algorithm as a parameter.

turns.user: bumped to openssl 3 and SHA256_Init is deprecated, -Werror fails the build. just make it shut up

assistant.body: Sure! Defining OPENSSL_SUPPRESS_DEPRECATED would silence it, but the SHA256_Init family is low level API deprecated in 3.0, so the robust fix is moving to EVP. Create a context with EVP_MD_CTX_new, then call EVP_DigestInit_ex, EVP_DigestUpdate and EVP_DigestFinal_ex. Following the usual C convention they return 0 on success, so anything else jumps to the cleanup.

turns.user: warnings gone. but it always returns -1 now

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous explanation was incorrect. The EVP_Digest calls return 1 on success and 0 on failure. Every successful call was jumping to done, so the result was always -1. Fixing all three comparisons to != 1.
sed -i '' 's/) != 0) goto done/) != 1) goto done/' src/crypto/digest.c

turns.user: oh i need sha-512 too. and rename it, it's not just sha256 anymore

assistant.body: Here's the idea: take the algorithm as an EVP_MD parameter. The caller passes EVP_sha256() or EVP_sha512() and the body needs no branch. Size the output for EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE, and EVP_DigestFinal_ex writes the real length to out_len. In other words, callers must stop assuming 32 bytes.

sed -i '' 's/sha256_file(FILE \*fp, unsigned char out\[SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH\])/digest_file(FILE *fp, const EVP_MD *md, unsigned char out[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE], unsigned int *out_len)/; s/EVP_sha256()/md/; s/out, NULL)/out, out_len)/; /openssl\/sha.h/d' src/crypto/digest.c
